e.etymology: A form of the biblical Azriel, Hebrew for God is my help, reflecting Ashkenazi pronunciation. It also fits the current taste for Ezra and Ezekiel.
The Latin word for evening and for the evening star, also the source of vespers, the evening prayer service. Ian Fleming gave it to Vesper Lynd in Casino Royale (1953).
namesakes: Vesper Lynd (James Bond's love interest in Casino Royale)

assoc.t: Vesper Lynd, Bond's love in Casino Royale
vespers, the evening prayer service
the Vesper martini, James Bond's cocktail

e.etymology: A Japanese girls' name whose meaning depends on the kanji chosen; mi is often written with the character for beautiful. In the US it has risen in the 2020s alongside names like Amori and Miyah.
A short form of Dorothy, Theodora and Isidora, all built on Greek doron, gift. It has stood as an independent name since the early 1800s.

assoc.t: Dora the Explorer, Nickelodeon cartoon heroine

e.etymology: The Spanish form of the Germanic name Rigobert, from elements meaning mighty and bright. Saint Rigobert was an 8th-century archbishop of Reims.
In early 20th-century America Arvin sat alongside Ervin, Irvin and the Scandinavian Arvid. Today it is also a Persian name and a short form of the Indian name Arvind.
A spelling of Muhammad, from Arabic hammada, to praise. It is the name of the prophet of Islam and one of the most common names in the world; this spelling is favored in Lebanon, Syria and Malaysia.

assoc.t: Muhammad, the prophet of Islam

e.meaning: sea and soar, or sea and the Big Dipper, depending on the kanji
e.etymology: A Japanese boys' name whose meaning depends on its kanji: kai is usually sea or ocean, and to may be soar or the Big Dipper. It has been among the most popular boys' names in Japan since the 2000s.

assoc.t: Kaito Kid, phantom thief in the anime Case Closed

e.etymology: The Latin word for sky or heaven, the root of celestial. Caelum is also a small southern constellation, there named for a different Latin caelum, an engraver's chisel.

assoc.t: Caelum, a faint southern constellation
Noctis Lucis Caelum, hero of Final Fantasy XV

e.etymology: A spelling of Isa, the Arabic name of Jesus in the Quran, where he is honored as a prophet. The double e shows the long vowel for English readers.
An English surname meaning son of Ever, a medieval short form of Everard, brave as a boar. As a first name it follows Everett and Emerson; Éverson is also a common given name in Brazil.
A clipped spelling of the color name Blue, and also the Italian word for blue. Blue itself gained ground after Beyoncé and Jay-Z named their daughter Blue Ivy in 2012.
namesakes: Blu (the blue macaw in the animated film Rio)

assoc.t: Blu-ray, the high-definition disc format
blu, e-cigarette brand
Blu, the macaw in the animated film Rio

e.etymology: A recent American name in the family of Ailani, Elani and Leilani, built on Hawaiian lani, sky or heaven. It also resembles Hebrew Ilan and Ilana, tree.
A pet form of Mary, in use since the 1700s: Mary became Molly, and Molly rhymed into Polly, the same way Meg became Peg. It is also used as a short form of Pauline and Paula.

assoc.t: stock name for a parrot, as in Polly want a cracker
Polly Pocket, Mattel's miniature doll line
Polly Put the Kettle On, nursery rhyme

e.etymology: An anglicized form of Irish Caolán, from caol, slender, with a diminutive ending. Keelan is also an Irish surname from Ó Céileacháin, from céile, companion.
From Hebrew Yechiel, may God live, borne by several Levites in the books of Chronicles, where English Bibles spell it Jehiel. It is used mainly in Orthodox Jewish families.
A Hawaiian name traditionally glossed as messenger of a chief; lani means sky, heaven or royalty. Disney chose it for its Aulani resort on Oahu, opened in 2011.

assoc.t: Aulani, Disney's resort and spa in Hawaii

e.etymology: The English word for clearness, from Latin claritas, brightness, and related to Clara and Claire. It is a modern virtue-style name in the mold of Charity and Verity.

assoc.t: Clarity, 2012 hit song by Zedd

e.etymology: The feminine of Arabic Mahir, skilled or expert. It is common in South Asia, where Pakistani film star Mahira Khan has made it familiar.
A spelling of Annabelle, which began in medieval Scotland as Annabel, an alteration of Amabel, from Latin amabilis, lovable. It is now usually heard as Anna plus French belle, beautiful.

assoc.t: Annabelle, haunted doll of the Conjuring films, by sound

e.etymology: A spelling of Colette, a French short form of Nicolette, the feminine of Nicholas, from Greek nike, victory, and laos, people. Saint Colette of Corbie reformed the Poor Clares in the 1400s.
namesakes: Toni Collette (Australian actress, The Sixth Sense and Hereditary)

e.etymology: A phonetic respelling of Cameron, the Scottish clan name from Gaelic cam sròn, crooked nose. This spelling peaked in 2008.
A spelling of Harlan, an English surname from a place name usually read as Old English hara, hare, plus land. Harlan spread in the US in honor of Supreme Court justice John Marshall Harlan.
A respelling of Lyric, the English word for the words of a song, from Greek lyrikos, sung to the lyre. Lyric became a given name in the 1990s.
In Russian, Vanya is the everyday pet form of Ivan, John, as in Chekhov's Uncle Vanya. In Bulgaria it is a women's name, and Indian families use Vanya from Sanskrit vana, forest.
namesakes: Uncle Vanya (title character of Chekhov's play)
Vanya Hargreeves (the violinist sibling in The Umbrella Academy)

assoc.t: Uncle Vanya, title role of Chekhov's play

e.note: In Russia Vanya is a boys' nickname, like Johnny; Americans give it mostly to girls.

e.etymology: The English word, from Old French sauveour and Latin salvator, one who saves, and a title of Jesus in Christianity. It matches Spanish Salvador and joins recent names like Messiah and Saint.

assoc.t: the Savior, a Christian title for Jesus

e.note: In Christian use the Savior means Jesus, so some people find it presumptuous as a personal name.

e.etymology: A pet form of Roberta and Robert, from the Germanic elements hrod, fame, and berht, bright. The -ie spelling has been the usual one for girls since the early 1900s.
namesakes: Bobbie Gentry (singer of Ode to Billie Joe)

assoc.t: Bobbie, organic infant formula brand

e.etymology: A spelling of Jada, a modern American name usually linked to jade, the green gemstone. Jada rose in the 1990s with actress Jada Pinkett Smith.

A spelling of Nia, Swahili for purpose and the fifth principle of Kwanzaa, adopted by Black American families from the 1970s. It also echoes Arabic niyyah, intention, and the ending of Aniyah and Saniyah.
From Hebrew tovah, good, the feminine of tov. A separate Swedish Tova is an old form of Tove, a Norse short form of names beginning with Thor, revived in Sweden in 1912.
From Hebrew Tzipporah, the feminine of tzippor, bird. In Exodus Zipporah is the Midianite wife of Moses and daughter of Jethro. Sephora is the Greek and Latin form.
namesakes: Zipporah (wife of Moses in the Book of Exodus)

e.etymology: The initials A.J. written as a name, usually standing for a first and middle name such as Anthony James or Andrew Joseph. It can also be a short spelling of the Indian name Ajay.
